newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL hoping second time lucky as pursues NZ Sky TV.
newsitem.headline: INL hoping second time lucky as pursues NZ Sky TV.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch-dominated New Zealand newspaper publisher, Independent Newspapers Ltd, said on Tuesday it was confident its second bid for a stake in Sky Network Television would be successful.

INL, 49.5 percent owned by Murdoch vehicle News Corp, was thwarted in February in its first attempt to buy a stake of 80 percent or more in Sky NZ -- which is unrelated to the Sky satellite tv firms controlled by Murdoch.
This time INL is only negotiating to buy U.S.-based HKP Partners' 51 percent stake in the network.
HKP is owned by U.S. telecom companies Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, firms which also each own a quarter stake in Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd.
Telecom is currently building up its own cable television network across New Zealand.

"We were always quite keen on purchasing a shareholding in Sky, we were not successful last time, but we kept the lines of communication open and we are back in negotiations and this time we feel there is an excellent chance of success," INL chief Executive Mike Robson told Reuters.
He said the fact that INL was only dealing with one company gave it more confidence of success. And INL would be comfortable with a 51 percent holding in the broadcast pay-tv operator.
Other shareholders in Sky include Television New Zealand, Heatley Jarvis Investments, Todd Corp and Tappenden Group.
A recent newspaper story said Sky TV was about to be floated and Robson, while not wishing to comment in detail, acknowledged that such a plan did not necessary conflict with INL's.
"That (a float) is a possibility," Robson said.
He declined to confirm a value on Sky put in the newspaper article at around NZ$800 million ($545 million).
But INL would not have to go to its shareholders to buy a 51 percent stake in Sky, Robson said.
"In the deal we are doing, the company would have absolutely no difficulties in financing at all. We wouldn't intend to go to shareholders with an issue," he said.
Asked why INL was so keen on Sky, Robson said it was well documented that INL had had an interest in television for some time.
He said Sky would also provide a useful distributor for sports content in which Murdoch, through other vehicles, had invested hundreds of millions of dollars.
"You can work out that our major shareholder is interested in this area (sport) and it is just another piece of synergy in the picture.
"But it is really an investment by INL in pay television that we are talking about," Robson added. ($=1.47NZ$)
